new.title: Climb to the Tour de Guinette above Étampes
new.desc: The Tour de Guinette is the surviving keep of Étampes' royal castle, built in the 12th century in the unusual form of a four-lobed quatrefoil. The town saved it in 1859 and it has been a listed monument since 1862, with a restoration campaign recently completed.
new.tip: Opening has been limited during restoration, so check the Étampes tourism office before going; the hilltop park around it gives a view over the town.
new.q: Tour de Guinette, Rue de la Tour de Guinette, Étampes

new.title: Step into the Collégiale Notre-Dame-du-Fort
new.desc: This collegiate church was founded in the early 11th century by King Robert the Pious and rebuilt in stages up to the 14th century. It has been a listed monument since 1970 and is known for its leaning Romanesque bell tower and its portal.
new.tip: Combine it with a stroll along the old streets of Étampes; the church is usually open in the afternoon.

new.title: Meet Tinguely's giant Cyclop in the forest
new.desc: Le Cyclop is a 22-metre sculpture covered in mirrors and scrap metal, built from 1969 to 1994 by Jean Tinguely, Niki de Saint Phalle and a team of artists. It reopened to the public in May 2022 after a year of restoration; the face and the gardens around it are free to see.
new.tip: Entry to the interior is by guided and paid visit only, on set days, so confirm the schedule with the Cyclop association before travelling.
new.q: Le Cyclop, Forêt de Milly, Milly-la-Forêt

new.title: Visit Cocteau's chapel Saint-Blaise-des-Simples
new.desc: The chapel is the last trace of a 12th-century leper hospice at Milly-la-Forêt. Jean Cocteau decorated its walls in 1959 with herbal 'simples' and a resurrection scene, and he is buried inside. It is a listed monument and a small garden of medicinal plants lies beside it.
new.tip: Opening is limited, mostly afternoons in season and heritage days, so check with the Milly tourist office.
new.q: Chapelle Saint-Blaise des Simples, Rue de l'Amiral de Graville, Milly-la-Forêt

new.title: Stand under the 1479 hall of Milly-la-Forêt
new.desc: The covered market hall on Place du Marché was built in 1479 on the orders of the local lord Louis Malet de Graville, with a huge oak frame on stone pillars. It has been a listed monument since 1923 and still shelters the Thursday afternoon market.
new.tip: Come on a Thursday afternoon for the market, and the antiques fair on the second Sunday of the month.
new.q: Halle de Milly-la-Forêt, Place du Marché, Milly-la-Forêt

new.title: Follow the canals of the Château de Courances
new.desc: Courances is a brick and stone château of the 16th and 17th centuries with a park famed for its spring-fed water: canals, mirror pools and a Japanese garden. The park was redesigned by Achille Duchêne around 1900 and the château is still privately owned.
new.tip: Open weekends and holidays from April to early November, 14:00 to 18:00. The château is visited by guided tour only and is closed in July and August, while the park stays open.
new.q: Château de Courances, Rue du Château, Courances

new.title: Cross the moat to Dourdan's Philip Augustus castle
new.desc: Dourdan is the last castle built by King Philip Augustus, around 1222, with a round keep modelled on the medieval Louvre. It became a royal prison in the 17th century and is now a Musée de France with a modern museum building in the courtyard.
new.tip: Open year-round except some closures, so check hours at chateau.dourdan.fr. The town's old market hall and streets are right next to it.
new.q: Château de Dourdan, Place du Général de Gaulle, Dourdan

new.title: Climb the medieval Tour de Montlhéry
new.desc: The 13th-century keep of the ruined Montlhéry castle stands on a hill and offers a panorama over Essonne. In 1849 the physicist Hippolyte Fizeau used the line between this tower and Paris-Montmartre in an experiment to measure the speed of light.
new.tip: Open on weekends from April to October and on heritage days; the climb is about 138 steps. Check hours with the Montlhéry town hall.
new.q: Tour de Montlhéry, Rue de la Tour, Montlhéry

new.title: Smell the plant gardens of the Conservatoire des plantes
new.desc: The Conservatoire national des plantes à parfum, médicinales, aromatiques et industrielles is a botanical garden and nursery created in 1987 at Milly-la-Forêt. Its labelled 'Jardin remarquable' presents some 600 aromatic, perfume and medicinal species and a Maison des simples.
new.tip: Guided walks and open days run in season, so check cnpmai.net; the garden is a short walk from the Cocteau chapel.
new.q: Conservatoire national des plantes à parfum, Chemin des Petits Saules, Milly-la-Forêt

new.title: Stroll the 98-hectare park of the Domaine de Chamarande
new.desc: The Louis XIII château of Chamarande, dating from 1654, sits in the largest public garden of Essonne, redesigned by landscape architect Jacques Sgard and labelled 'Jardin remarquable'. The département bought it in 1978 and it now hosts contemporary art and the archives.
new.tip: Entry to the park is free and it is open daily; the château only opens for exhibitions. It is reachable by RER C at Chamarande.
new.q: Domaine de Chamarande, Rue du Commandant Arnoux, Chamarande

new.title: Wander the picturesque follies of the Domaine de Méréville
new.desc: This 58-hectare Anglo-Chinese garden was created from 1784 by the banker marquis de Laborde with architect François-Joseph Bélanger and painter Hubert Robert. It was open to the public in 2018 and labelled 'Jardin remarquable' in 2019, with bridges, a colonnade and a river.
new.tip: Free-entry walks on weekends and holidays in season, guided tours via the Méréville tourist office; confirm the current hours before travelling.
new.q: Domaine départemental de Méréville, Le Mérévillois

new.title: Hunt rare plants at the Saint-Jean-de-Beauregard plant fair
new.desc: The 17th-century Château de Saint-Jean-de-Beauregard hosts the Fête des Plantes, a spring and autumn gathering of more than 200 nurseries and plant artisans from across Europe. The autumn fair celebrated its 40th year in 2024.
new.tip: Held over a long weekend in April and again in late September; buy tickets in advance and bring a trolley.

new.title: Watch vintage aircraft at Le Temps des Hélices
new.desc: Each Pentecost weekend the Amicale Jean-Baptiste Salis stages its air meeting at the Cerny-La Ferté-Alais airfield, with historic propeller aircraft and warbirds in the air. The 53rd edition took place on 23 and 24 May 2026 and drew over 30,000 visitors.
new.tip: Book tickets ahead and arrive early because roads fill up; the date follows Pentecost each year.
new.q: Aérodrome de Cerny La Ferté-Alais, Cerny

new.title: Pick your own fruit at the Cueillette de Torfou
new.desc: The Cueillette de Torfou in the Juine valley is a 20-hectare pick-your-own farm owned by the Poupinel family for four generations. Visitors harvest seasonal fruit and vegetables themselves.
new.tip: Open in the growing season; check the farm's current hours and what is ripe before going.

new.title: Buy Méréville watercress at the Villa Paul cressonnière
new.desc: The Cressonnière de la Villa Paul in Méréville is run by the Barberot family and grows the watercress known as the green gold of Essonne. It sells from a shop on the farm and at markets, and runs visits of the beds.
new.tip: Open on weekdays, with weekends by appointment only; the cress is best in cold months and goes well in soup.
new.q: Cressonnière de la Villa Paul, Route de Courcelles, Méréville

new.title: Dine at Les Coqs on Milly's market square
new.desc: Les Coqs, at 24 place du Marché in Milly-la-Forêt, is a restaurant listed in the Michelin Guide and rated 12/20 by Gault&Millau, with chef Émilien Le Normand. It won four Papilles d'Or in 2020.
new.tip: Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays; book ahead, especially at weekends.
new.q: Les Coqs, 24 Place du Marché, Milly-la-Forêt

new.title: Eat a modern bistro menu at Le Pieux in Étampes
new.desc: Le Pieux, at 91 rue de la République in Étampes, is a bistro by chef Marc Wang listed by Gault&Millau, serving traditional French cooking with careful technique. Gault&Millau describes it as a bistro of good standing at modest prices.
new.tip: Set menus start around 15 to 26 euros; book for weekend dinners.
new.q: Le Pieux, 91 Rue de la République, Étampes
